section_summary: This section records Japanese merchant-vessel movements, cargoes, fuel, mail and passengers across Pacific and South American ports in 1941. It also contains repeated letters warning about Japanese fishing vessels near Alaska, a naval shipping report, and Philippine oil companies’ reports on supplies to foreign vessels. Many telegrams are followed by copies or paraphrases sent to the Navy.

subfiles.title: Gearhart letter forwarding Miscovich’s warning, first copy
subfiles.about: Forwards John Miscovich’s letter about Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Gearhart endorses Miscovich’s reliability and forwards his warning.

subfiles.title: Miscovich warning about Japanese fishing vessels, first copy
subfiles.about: Reports alleged Japanese fishing-vessel activity and urges a Pacific coastal patrol.
subfiles.summary: Miscovich lists Japanese boats said to operate in U.S. waters or head toward Alaska. He reports alleged links among fishing interests, cannery workers and Japanese officials, and urges control of the fishing fleet and a coastal patrol. His claims are presented as information received from others.

subfiles.title: Gearhart letter forwarding Miscovich’s warning, second copy
subfiles.about: Forwards another copy of Miscovich’s letter.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover letter endorsing Miscovich and forwarding his warning.

subfiles.title: Miscovich warning about Japanese fishing vessels, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats allegations about Japanese fishing vessels near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: A second copy lists vessels reportedly working in U.S. waters or bound for Alaska. It describes the Minato Maru and alleged Japanese fishing interests, then calls for a coastal patrol.

subfiles.title: Gearhart letter forwarding Miscovich’s warning, third copy
subfiles.about: Forwards a third copy of Miscovich’s letter.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover letter endorsing Miscovich and forwarding his warning.

subfiles.title: Miscovich warning about Japanese fishing vessels, third copy
subfiles.about: Repeats warnings about Japanese fishing craft and Alaska.
subfiles.summary: A third copy names Japanese boats reportedly in U.S. waters or approaching Alaska. Miscovich relays unverified claims about Japanese personnel and asks for a coastal patrol.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal to Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends the Gearhart and Miscovich letters for Coast Guard information.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the letters concerning Japanese boats in U.S. waters.

subfiles.title: Norfolk Maru at Valparaíso
subfiles.about: Reports Norfolk Maru’s arrival and onward route.
subfiles.summary: Norfolk Maru arrived from Buenos Aires on September 11 and sailed for Japan via Huasco, Peruvian ports and Manta.

subfiles.title: Noto Maru arrives at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports Noto Maru’s arrival from Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Noto Maru arrived directly from Yokohama on September 13.

subfiles.title: Noto Maru sails unexpectedly
subfiles.about: Reports Noto Maru’s sudden departure and revised mail count.
subfiles.summary: Noto Maru sailed without taking fuel; Hoyt corrected the unloaded mail count to 2,652 sacks, mostly for the United States.

subfiles.title: Noto Maru cargo and passengers
subfiles.about: Details Noto Maru’s unloaded cargo, passengers and expected route.
subfiles.summary: The ship unloaded medicines, dyes and mail. Syunzi Sato and Count Di Sanmarzano disembarked; Hoyt expected the vessel to fuel and sail for Callao.

subfiles.title: Heiyo Maru anchors at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports Heiyo Maru’s arrival.
subfiles.summary: Heiyo Maru anchored at Manzanillo.

subfiles.title: Rakuto departs Bangkok
subfiles.about: Reports Rakuto’s departure for Swatow.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese vessel Rakuto departed September 15 for Swatow.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessel movements at Bangkok
subfiles.about: Reports movements of Batavia and Nissyo.
subfiles.summary: Batavia arrived September 12, and Nissyo departed September 14.

subfiles.title: Japanese shipping agents’ changing instructions
subfiles.about: Reports measures apparently intended to obscure Japanese ship movements.
subfiles.summary: Jenkins says instructions to Bolivian shipping agents change ship names, give departure dates at short notice and omit exact arrival dates. He suggests Japanese concern about possible hostilities as an explanation, without claiming to know whether hostilities are planned.

subfiles.title: Heiyo Maru prepares to sail
subfiles.about: Reports Heiyo Maru fueling, loading and expected departure.
subfiles.summary: Heiyo Maru took fuel and water, with passengers and resin to load, and was expected to sail for Yokohama September 18.

subfiles.title: Heiyo Maru sails for Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports Heiyo Maru’s departure.
subfiles.summary: Heiyo Maru sailed from Manzanillo for Yokohama at 6 p.m.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report on Japanese shipping at Manzanillo
subfiles.from: Frederick S. Leek; J. D. Conover Jr.
subfiles.about: Records Japanese vessel movements and strategic cargoes through Manzanillo in July.
subfiles.summary: The report lists Japanese ships arriving from Los Angeles or Valparaíso and departing onward in July 1941. It details cargoes including mica, molybdenum, tungsten, fluorspar, lead, mercury, scrap metal, tin plate and cotton. It also gives a cumulative estimate of mercury shipped from Mexico to Japan since January.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Toyooka Maru’s destination
subfiles.about: Requests Toyooka Maru’s destination after leaving Bombay.
subfiles.summary: Asks where Toyooka Maru sailed on September 12.

subfiles.title: Toyooka Maru destination
subfiles.about: Answers the inquiry about Toyooka Maru.
subfiles.summary: Toyooka Maru went to Cutchkundla and was scheduled to proceed to Karachi.

subfiles.title: Heiyo Maru cargo and passengers
subfiles.about: Supplies detailed Heiyo Maru loading and passenger information.
subfiles.summary: Hoyt lists fuel, water, resin, turpentine, cotton, lubricating oil and bronze manufactures loaded at Manzanillo. Six passengers disembarked and 112 embarked. The report names German and Japanese passengers and repeats allegations about some passengers’ official or intelligence roles.

subfiles.title: Terukawa and Toa Maru sailings
subfiles.about: Clarifies sailings from Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa departed September 15 for Manzanillo with Wakasugi aboard. Toa had sailed September 1 for Valparaíso; Linnell reported no sailings for the United States.

subfiles.title: Norfolk Maru at Antofagasta
subfiles.about: Reports Norfolk Maru’s arrival and departure.
subfiles.summary: Norfolk Maru arrived from Caldera September 17 and sailed for Huanillos and Peruvian ports September 21.

subfiles.title: Noto Maru at Callao
subfiles.about: Reports Noto Maru’s Callao call.
subfiles.summary: Noto Maru arrived September 22 from Kobe and sailed September 23 for Valparaíso via Mollendo.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché message on Heiyo Maru
subfiles.about: Records a received naval attaché message concerning Heiyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is largely illegible; it identifies a naval attaché message about Heiyo Maru.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner’s correspondence envelope
subfiles.about: Encloses correspondence from Manila.
subfiles.summary: Envelope for the following Manila oil-company reports.

subfiles.title: Tide Water sales to Japanese fishermen
subfiles.from: E. G. Hoffman, Tide Water Associated Oil Company
subfiles.about: Reports August diesel sales to Japanese fishermen.
subfiles.summary: One customer operating three launches bought 26.1 tons of diesel fuel.

subfiles.title: Caltex marine petroleum sales
subfiles.about: Lists fuel and lubricant sales to vessels during August.
subfiles.summary: Caltex itemizes bunker fuel and lubricants supplied to named vessels and explains adjustments to July invoices.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum sales to foreign vessels
subfiles.from: L. L. Rocke, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Reports August supplies to Japanese and French vessels.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese vessels received supplies; two French vessels received fuel.

subfiles.title: Asiatic Petroleum report of no deliveries
subfiles.about: Reports August fuel and lubricant deliveries.
subfiles.summary: The company made no deliveries to French or Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Terukawa Maru
subfiles.about: Asks about Terukawa Maru’s reported sailing and destination.
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification of a reported sailing from Yokohama toward South America.

subfiles.title: Toa Maru at Callao
subfiles.about: Reports Toa Maru’s Callao arrival and departure.
subfiles.summary: Toa Maru arrived September 28 from Yokohama and sailed September 29 for Rio de Janeiro via Valparaíso.

subfiles.title: Sakito Maru tows Arima Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Sakito Maru and Arima Maru at Callao.
subfiles.summary: Sakito Maru arrived towing Arima Maru from Mollendo, then sailed for Yokohama via Zorritos.

subfiles.title: Azuma Maru sails from Kobe
subfiles.about: Confirms Azuma Maru’s departure toward Manzanillo.
subfiles.summary: The Mexican consul general reported Azuma Maru sailed from Kobe September 14 for Manzanillo.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Azuma Maru
subfiles.about: Seeks confirmation of Azuma Maru’s departure.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Azuma Maru had departed for Manzanillo.

subfiles.title: Expected arrivals at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Gives expected arrival dates for Terukawa and Azuma Maru.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa was not expected before October 6; Azuma was expected between October 3 and 6.

subfiles.title: Norfolk Maru at Callao
subfiles.about: Reports Norfolk Maru’s Callao call and route to Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Norfolk Maru arrived October 2 and sailed October 3 for Kobe via Chancay.

subfiles.title: Noto Maru at Valparaíso
subfiles.about: Reports Noto Maru’s arrival and departure.
subfiles.summary: Noto Maru arrived from Arica September 28 and sailed for Japan via Tocopilla October 3.

subfiles.title: Azuma Maru arrives at Manzanillo, two copies
subfiles.about: Reports Azuma Maru’s arrival and unloaded goods.
subfiles.summary: Azuma Maru arrived October 3 from Japan and unloaded general merchandise, artificial silk and 436 sacks of mail.

subfiles.title: Azuma Maru disembarking passengers
subfiles.about: Names Japanese military and diplomatic passengers landing at Manzanillo.
subfiles.summary: Hoyt names seven Japanese officers or diplomatic staff who disembarked from Azuma Maru, with their reported posts in Washington and Mexico City. Five Mexican diplomats also returned from Japan.

subfiles.title: Terukawa reaches Acapulco
subfiles.about: Relays notice of Terukawa’s arrival at Acapulco.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa arrived from Japan at 6 p.m. October 5.

subfiles.title: Toa Maru at Valparaíso
subfiles.about: Reports Toa Maru’s South American route.
subfiles.summary: Toa Maru arrived from Callao October 4 and sailed October 5 toward Rio via Punta Arenas and Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: Terukawa anchors at Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports Terukawa Maru’s arrival.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa Maru anchored at Manzanillo October 7.

subfiles.title: Terukawa departs Acapulco; Wakasugi travels onward
subfiles.about: Reports Terukawa’s route and Kaname Wakasugi’s travel.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa left Acapulco October 6 for Manzanillo and South America. Wakasugi disembarked and flew from Mexico City toward Brownsville.

subfiles.title: Terukawa passengers
subfiles.about: Lists Terukawa passengers and their destinations.
subfiles.summary: Hoyt names passengers bound for Callao and Valparaíso, notes where they boarded, and reports Yoshikiyo Arimori’s disembarkation at Manzanillo.

subfiles.title: Azuma Maru embarks passengers and sails
subfiles.about: Lists embarking Japanese passengers and Azuma Maru’s departure.
subfiles.summary: Japanese passengers including a diplomat, air officer and military official boarded for Yokohama. Azuma Maru sailed for Callao at 5 p.m.

subfiles.title: Terukawa departs Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports Terukawa Maru’s departure, cargo and fueling.
subfiles.summary: Terukawa sailed for Pimentel after unloading paint and glass and taking 900 tons of fuel oil. It refused outbound cargo at the last minute.
